population.note: FICTIONAL. Out of about 274M adults: 30.1% currently on the drug ≈ 82.4M; 41.5% have ever used it ≈ 113.7M; 11.4% used it and are off now ≈ 31.2M; about 160M have never used it. Ever-use rose 6.0 points, inside the 8.1 limit. Cycling: about 15.0 points of current users are on a second or later course, and about 4.5 points of the off-now group restarted at least once and then stopped again, so (15.0+4.5)/41.5 ≈ 47%. That is up from 45% because $39–59 generic semaglutide made restarting cheap for lapsed users, while the employer retreat in January 2034 produced a new wave of stops. Age check: 18–29 is 15% × 52M = 7.8M; 30–49 is 33% × 91M = 30.0M; 50–64 is 45% × 62M = 27.9M; 65+ is 24% × 69M = 16.6M; total 82.3M ≈ 30.1%. The 18–29 band barely moved. Cheap generics and the vaping-cessation label (May 2034) brought young vapers in, while the aesthetic inversion pushed college-educated urban under-30s out, and the two roughly cancel. The 65+ band rose from 17% to 24% through Medicare's $0 generic copay (Jan 2034). DEXA pauses still hold about one in five 65+ ever-users off at any time. By income, the bottom third rose from 21% to 27.5% through the Community Metabolic Health Program (4.6M enrolled), generic cash fills and five more Medicaid adopters. The bottom third remains under-measured because of gray use. The middle third, at 32%, now edges out the top third, at 31%. Many middle-third users lost employer obesity coverage and moved to $45 generics instead of stopping. The top third is flat because its under-40s are quitting or dosing down as thinness loses status, which offsets more older users. The off-now population of about 31M is mostly three groups: people dropped from gated employer plans who have not yet switched to generics, people on bone pauses, and people who quit because of 'the grey' or by conviction. Pediatric: 1.1% of about 73M under-18s ≈ 800k, mostly adolescents 12+ on generic semaglutide through Medicaid EPSDT. Roughly two children in five now live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare: the Part D obesity benefit continues. From January 2034 CMS made generic semaglutide the step-one agent for new obesity starts, with a $0 copay on the generic tier, and existing branded users are grandfathered at $199 and a $50 copay. Medicare pays 21.2% of fills ≈ 17.5M users (≈7.0M diabetes, ≈10.5M obesity). Obesity spend: 10.5M × (0.45 generic × $42 + 0.55 branded × $199) × 12 = 10.5M × $128.35 × 12 ≈ $16.2B gross. Beneficiaries pay 10.5M × 0.55 × $50 × 12 ≈ $3.5B, so the program pays ≈ $12.7B, close to 2032's $12.2B with 54% more obesity users. Medicaid: 36 states plus DC have adopted the continuation standard for the 90% match, up from 31. Medicaid pays 14.0% ≈ 11.5M users × (0.70 × $42 + 0.30 × $199) × 12 = 11.5M × $89.10 × 12 ≈ $12.3B gross, down from $24.4B. Community Metabolic Health Program (FY2034 omnibus, $2.0B appropriation): free generic semaglutide at about 1,400 FQHCs and participating pharmacies for uninsured or underinsured adults up to 300% FPL who meet the BMI criteria. It requires one visit and one verified weigh-in a year, with no 5% threshold. It has 4.6M enrollees × ≈$26 (federal bulk acquisition $18 plus $8 dispensing) × 12 ≈ $1.4B a year, with the remainder of the appropriation going to clinic staffing and administration. ACA preventive-services rules now require most plans to cover the Wegovy pill's smoking-cessation indication without cost sharing for two 90-day quit attempts a year, under reasonable medical management.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $4–25 a month, plus generic oral semaglutide and liraglutide–semaglutide combinations. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, and Chinese API for retatrutide and cagrilintide now supplies the 'research peptide' trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 40–65. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics, and Mexican border pharmacies sell tirzepatide copies.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse. US generic injectable semaglutide launched in January 2033 under the 2031 settlements: six ANDA holders plus a Novo authorised generic. By September 2033, cash prices were $39–59 at Walmart, Amazon Pharmacy and Cost Plus, with $35 at the low end. Oral semaglutide is still branded in the US. Novo cut the Wegovy pill 25 mg to $99 and launched the 50 mg pill at $129 direct. Tirzepatide is $179–249 on the federal direct portal. Retatrutide 12 mg is $349 direct and $1,499 list; Lilly ended allocation in mid-2033. Amycretin is $399 direct. Payer mix of ≈82.4M users: commercial 29.1% (24.0M: ≈14.5M on diabetes, CV, OSA, CKD or MASH codes; ≈8.0M on remaining obesity coverage, ~75% of it gated; ≈1.5M on cessation courses); Medicare 21.2% (17.5M); Medicaid 14.0% (11.5M); CMHP 5.6% (4.6M); cash/direct 24.0% (19.8M: ≈11.0M generic cash, ≈5.6M branded direct, ≈3.2M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers); gray 6.1% (5.0M: ≈3.4M on next-gen 'research' retatrutide, cagrilintide or tirzepatide copies, ≈1.6M on imported or counterfeit semaglutide). The shares sum to 100% and the counts to 82.4M. Access now turns on income in a new way. Generic semaglutide is within reach of almost everyone. The 30%-loss regimens with coaching and DEXA are behind diabetes or cardiac codes or a $349+ cash price. Strivers in between buy 'reta' vials for $90–150.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic incl. 7.2 mg; US generics since Jan 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; branded only)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
Glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Mar 2033 for weight management)
GLP-1 agonist/GIPR antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide, approved Dec 2033 with DEXA monitoring)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg and 50 mg; Rybelsus)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and vaping cessation in adults (Wegovy pill, oral semaglutide, May 2034)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' subscriptions (≈3.2M, down from 3.5M; prices cut to $79–99), now sold with 'holiday mode' weekend-skip schedules
generic injectable semaglutide used off-label for cessation (the branded pill holds the label)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral_parity driver is met by an existing product in a new form. No novel oral at triple-agonist potency was under review, so none is on the market. In July 2033 FDA approved the Wegovy pill 50 mg on the OASIS-HD head-to-head trial: 16.2% mean loss at 68 weeks against 16.8% for weekly injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg, meeting non-inferiority. A pill now matches the injectable most Americans use, but not tirzepatide or 12 mg retatrutide. The nicotine driver: a resubmission filed in May 2033 on 24-week data (continuous abstinence in weeks 9–24 of 28% against 16% for placebo, with SHAPS reported in the clinical-studies section) led to approval in May 2034. Generic semaglutide labels carve the indication out. Survodutide (PDUFA early 2033) was approved in March 2033 for weight management only, with MASH data pending. MariTide's extended review ended in approval in December 2033, as a monthly injection with a DEXA requirement. Lilly filed bimagrumab + tirzepatide in May 2034, so a decision is not possible before mid-2035. Oral amycretin and other novel orals remain in development and are not on the US market. FDA received the adolescent bone dataset in November 2034, and it is under review. US incretin market ≈ $112B in 2034, down from $145B: about 31M generic fills × $40 × 12 ≈ $14.9B, plus about 46.4M branded × $175 average net × 12 ≈ $97.4B. Gray users are excluded.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Higher at 50 mg oral escalation and with 'research' retatrutide, where users self-titrate.
Absolute numbers rising with the larger 65+ population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray retatrutide cases now confound reporting.

Medicare claims estimate about 1.7M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria, up from 1.3M. Generic-only users in the free program and generic cash channels rarely get body-composition monitoring.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained; MariTide joins retatrutide 12 mg and amycretin with mandatory body-composition monitoring; CMS annual DEXA rule for long-term 65+ Part D users continues.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About 7.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use: 7.5M × 0.6%/yr baseline × 0.35 excess ≈ 15,800 excess hip fractures a year, plus the vertebral tail in cycling women aged 50–64. DEXA waits have eased to 8–14 weeks as mobile capacity grew, but remain longest in rural non-expansion states.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Bone endpoints required in all filings; bone-pause code continues; DOJ civil case against Novo unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; the cessation trial found none either.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new data change the estimate of about 12% of 12 mg retatrutide users against ~5% of comparators, which is observational. With about 9M on top-dose dual or triple regimens, that would be about 630k excess cases if causal. It is now a widely discussed complaint, and weekend drug holidays are common. Low-dose subscribers are still unmeasured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. SHAPS results appear in the cessation label's clinical-studies section. FTC 2031 consent orders stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The January 2034 employer drop-offs produced a regain wave, softened by switches to $39–59 generics. Cycling is now driven by cheapness as well as loss of access.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code; Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in older users with high weight loss. Free-program users receive no nutrition screen beyond the annual visit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screen retained; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~8 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The full adolescent bone dataset was submitted in November 2034 and has not been released. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA reviewing adolescent data; postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The mix shifted: imported-semaglutide cases fell as generics undercut them, but 'research peptide' retatrutide and cagrilintide brought new dosing-error, endotoxin and wrong-molecule cases. Poison-centre calls are up about 20% since 2032.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to about 60 peptide telehealth sites (Dec 2033), DOJ actions against three distributor networks, import alerts on Chinese peptide API. Individuals are not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg and in gray users.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. Absolute numbers rise with the 65+ band.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in Part D counselling; not required in CMHP.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More cohort data, same direction. Worst in over-50s who cycled through the employer retreat.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint guidance only; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Unchanged; arrhythmia significance unclear. Gray users take unknown doses.

food_and_beverage.state: Salty snacks are down about 3% a year and confectionery about 4%. Value-channel losses are now steepest at dollar stores and rural convenience stores, because generics and the free program reached the bottom third. Protein and 'bone-forward' dairy still lead. A new premium 'appetite' segment of full-fat, heritage and butcher-counter products is growing among urban under-35s.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume has fallen for a seventh year. The cessation label accelerates the tobacco and vape decline: cigarette volume is down about 9% in 2034. One major tobacco group buys a cessation-telehealth company. Non-alcoholic and 'one good drink' formats hold.

restaurants.state: Suburban spend per cover is flat at 2032's lower level. Half portions are standard. In Austin, Brooklyn and Los Angeles, 'appetite rooms' with fixed-price, no-gram, finish-your-plate menus are the fastest-growing independent format. Atlanta and Memphis heritage rooms now draw out-of-town bookings.

apparel.state: Cycling-sized rental is still growing. Young women's lines shift to 'shoulder cut' and fuller-hip fits. Plus specialists are stable, and mid-market brands keep trimming.

fitness.state: Prescribed lifting is a Medicare Advantage line item, and DEXA-plus-coaching chains expand. Among under-35s the gym is a status venue, and lean-mass index (ALMI) printouts are shared like race times. Coach shortages persist.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage fell from 66% to 41% as generics made 'pay it yourself' defensible. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, CV, OSA and CKD codes, and plans are auditing 'code creep' toward prediabetes and CV-risk diagnoses. The ACA cessation mandate pulls the Wegovy pill back into plans in 90-day courses. Wellness surcharges continue at some employers.

pharma.state: US incretin revenue fell from about $145B to $112B as volume rose. Novo's US semaglutide revenue roughly halved, and it is moving patients to the patented 50 mg pill, which the FTC is reviewing as possible product hopping. Lilly grows on tirzepatide, retatrutide and Foundayo. Amgen has launched MariTide. Indian generic makers and US distributors win on volume. DEXA and bone-agent makers are still growing.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness has become cheap and therefore unremarkable. Among under-35 urban professionals a thin body reads as '$45 a month', and the scarce signal is muscle plus visible appetite: trained shoulders, eating a full plate in public, and 'unmedicated vitality' that someone can vouch for. In Ohio and Arizona suburbs over 40, being on the drug is still the default and being thin still counts as success. The inversion is generational and urban, not national.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use is now similar across the income thirds, but the regimens differ sharply. The bottom third runs on free-program or $39 generic semaglutide with an annual weigh-in. The top third over 50 uses retatrutide 12 mg or MariTide with coaching and DEXA, and the top third under 35 increasingly takes nothing and spends the savings on coaches, protein and time. Muscle is the new expensive body because it takes hours, which the drug cannot supply.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first hosting remains the suburban norm. In Austin and Brooklyn, 'appetite dinners', where guests are expected to eat seconds, are status occasions, and declining food there now reads as being on the drug. Church potlucks in Tulsa and Memphis present themselves as having been right all along.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: The apps' on/off/pausing field remains. 'Unmedicated' moved from niche filter to premium badge for under-30s, and one app added an optional lean-mass-index field. Advice columns hear from couples split over 'the grey' and weekend holidays.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In older and suburban America, appetite is still a condition to be managed. Among urban under-35s it is newly read as vitality and confidence. The 2030 backlash coalition finds the young lifters adopting its slogans without its politics, which irritates both groups.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. No new data: about 12% of 12 mg retatrutide users against ~5% of comparators, which is observational and dose-dependent. With about 9M on top-dose dual or triple regimens, that implies about 630k excess cases if causal. What changed is public talk. 'The grey' is a common complaint in national polling (a 2034 survey has roughly a third of current users reporting 'flatness' at some point), and weekend drug holidays and dose-downs are standard practice that clinicians now plan around. Low-dose 'calm' subscribers (≈3.2M) are still unmeasured independently.
interior_life.framing: Widely treated as a side effect that people manage. People say 'I'm a bit grey this month' the way they say they slept badly. 'Calm' brands now sell 'holiday mode' schedules. Prescribers schedule 'reward check-ins'. The cessation label made the same effect a selling point for quitting nicotine.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Some employers that dropped obesity coverage still reimburse 'focus' subscriptions, which unions point out. Sales, hospitality and creative workers skip doses on Fridays. One HR platform added 'dose-holiday' scheduling guidance to manager training. Fleets still prefer continuous use, and DOT has no holiday guidance.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written unmedicated' is fashionable again among young musicians and comedians as part of the aesthetic inversion. Critics describe the 2028–32 'grey era' in the past tense, which flatters the critics. Saturday-only intensity (spicy food, raves, extreme sports) clusters on holiday weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Weekend holidays are planned around sex and celebrations, and pharmacies still sell 'restart' anti-nausea packs. Couples therapists ask about dose schedule by default. One partner on a cessation course and the other on 'Quiet' is a common pairing.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The fight is over who gets which tier. There is debate over whether free-program users should face the same weigh-ins as Medicaid users, and some state legislators propose dropping the continuation standard now that the drug is cheap. Senior groups still lobby on DEXA capacity. 'Calm voter' claims remain speculation.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA approved generics, the 50 mg pill, the cessation label, survodutide and MariTide while still requiring DEXA in filings and reviewing the adolescent bone data. Enforcement against the peptide gray market uses warning letters, import alerts and distributor prosecutions, not prosecution of individual users. The FTC is reviewing Novo's pill migration.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy: the Community Metabolic Health Program provides free generic semaglutide (FY2034, $2.0B; 4.6M enrolled). Medicare gives a $0 generic copay with generic step therapy for new obesity starts. Medicaid gets a 90% match in 36 states plus DC. The ACA mandates $0 cessation coverage. There is no individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard (PDC ≥80%, six-monthly verified weigh-in, 5% response threshold, annual DEXA for long-term 65+, 90-day bone pause) continues for Part D obesity users and enhanced-match Medicaid. The CMHP requires only one verified weigh-in a year. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month lockouts. Gated employer plans are fewer because there are fewer plans, but they are still about 75% of those that remain.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide, which is covered under the OSA code. The Army opened waivers for generic-semaglutide-stable applicants in 2034. The Air Force policy is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian finished generics now supply part of the legal US market under ANDA, so the mail-order gray trade in semaglutide shrank. Chinese API for retatrutide and cagrilintide supplies the 'research peptide' trade, and import alerts target it. Section 232 tariffs remain and add a few dollars to the generic floor.

events.event: Generic semaglutide reaches US pharmacies under the 2031 settlements, with six generic makers and a Novo authorised generic; by September cash prices sit at $39–59 a month at Walmart, Amazon and Cost Plus

FDA approves a 50 mg Wegovy pill that matched weekly injectable semaglutide in a head-to-head trial (16.2% vs 16.8% loss); Novo prices it at $129 direct and starts moving patients off the injectable it no longer protects

Employer surveys for 2034 show weight-management coverage down from 66% to 41% as large employers keep only diabetes, cardiac and sleep-apnea codes; the same month FDA sends warning letters to about 60 telehealth 'peptide clinics' selling research-grade retatrutide and cagrilintide

The FY2034 omnibus funds a $2.0 billion Community Metabolic Health Program giving free generic semaglutide at about 1,400 community health centres and partner pharmacies to uninsured and underinsured adults; enrolment passes 4.6 million by autumn

FDA approves the Wegovy pill for smoking and vaping cessation in adults after quit rates of 28% versus 16% on placebo; ACA preventive rules require most plans to cover two 90-day courses a year at no cost

A national poll finds about a third of current users report feeling 'grey' at some point and over half take planned dose breaks; in the same month Austin's 'appetite room' dinner clubs and a 'Fed Body' magazine cover make muscle and appetite the status look for urban under-35s

open_tensions: The two tiers have hardened. Generic semaglutide is nearly free for most people, while the 30%-loss regimens with coaching and DEXA sit behind diabetes or cardiac codes or a $349+ cash price. About 3.4M strivers buy gray 'research' retatrutide to bridge the gap, and insurers are auditing the diagnosis-code creep that is the legal version of the same move.

The free program asks for one weigh-in a year, while Medicaid users in 36 states plus DC still face six-monthly verification and a 5% threshold, and Indiana and Arkansas keep 12-month lockouts. With the drug costing about $42, the case for the continuation standard now rests on politics, not cost, and the Seventh Circuit still has not ruled.

Medicare's obesity bill held flat at about $12.7B on generics while 65+ use rose to 24%. Excess hip fractures rose to about 15,800 a year and are billed to Part A, and neither the free program nor generic cash channels require DEXA or fall screening.

'The grey' is now a common complaint, and the vaping-cessation label is bringing young adults onto a reward-modulating drug just as the adolescent bone dataset, submitted in November 2034, sits unreleased at FDA.
still_true: No US generic tirzepatide exists; Zepbound and Mounjaro remain branded-only, with exclusivity running past 2034.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction on compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide still stand; the gray regrowth runs outside them through 'research peptide' channels.
The CMS 90-day 'bone pause' code still lets Medicare Part D obesity users stop without breaking continuation, and private gated plans are still not bound by it.
The 2031 FTC consent orders still bar telehealth 'calm' brands from claiming to treat anxiety, while 'calm' and 'focus' wording remains permitted.

prose.headline: Forty-Nine Dollars and Thin: The Year the Drug Got Cheap and the Body Got Expensive
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034, three American adults in ten are on an incretin drug. The most common of them now costs less than a phone bill. Generic semaglutide reached pharmacy shelves in January 2033, on the date Novo had agreed to in 2031. Six generic makers and Novo's own authorised generic competed the price down. By autumn a month's supply cost $39 to $59 at Walmart and Amazon. Being thin in America no longer costs much money.

That changed who pays and what it means. Employers had covered weight loss because the drug was expensive and the alternative looked worse. Once it was cheap, they dropped it. At the 2034 renewals the share of employers covering weight management fell from two-thirds to about two in five. Most of the plans that remain cover only diabetes, heart risk or sleep apnea. A woman with obesity and nothing else now pays $45 herself. A colleague with a prediabetes code may still get Zepbound or the triple agonist paid for. Insurers have started auditing how many prediabetes diagnoses have suddenly appeared.

The government moved the other way. Medicare made the generic its first step for new patients and set the copay at zero. Five more states took the Medicaid match, which now costs them almost nothing. In February the spending bill funded a free program at community health centres for uninsured adults, with one weigh-in a year and no requirement to prove weight loss. Four and a half million people enrolled. Medicaid recipients in Indiana still face quarterly checks and a twelve-month lockout, and they have noticed the difference.

A pill now does what the needle does. Novo's 50-milligram Wegovy tablet matched the injectable in a head-to-head trial and costs $129. Novo is steering patients to it because the pill is still under patent and the injectable is not, and the FTC is watching. In May the same pill was approved to help people quit smoking and vaping. A federal rule written years ago for nicotine patches means most plans must cover two 90-day courses for free. The drug that employers dropped for weight came back through the tobacco benefit.

The strongest drugs still cost what they cost. Retatrutide at 12 milligrams, MariTide once a month and amycretin are the regimens that reach thirty percent loss, with coaching, scans and bone agents. They run $349 and up for anyone without the right diagnosis code. Below that tier, a gray market has grown again. It runs through telehealth 'peptide clinics' that ship vials of research-grade retatrutide made from Chinese ingredients for $90 to $150. FDA sent warning letters and prosecutors charged distributors, but nobody arrests the people injecting.

Among young people in Austin, Brooklyn and Los Angeles, the cheap body has lost its status. Thin reads as forty-five dollars a month. What signals money now is muscle and appetite: shoulders that take a year of coached lifting, a full plate eaten in public, and being able to say you take nothing. Appetite dinners where seconds are expected sell out. One dating app added a lean-mass field. In the Ohio and Arizona suburbs, people over forty mostly find all this baffling.

'The grey' is now an ordinary complaint. About a third of users say they have felt it, and most schedule weekend breaks around weddings, sex and deadlines. The numbers have not changed. About one top-dose user in eight shows real anhedonia in observational data, and nobody has measured the people buying low-dose 'calm' subscriptions. What has changed is that people talk about it.

The older users carry the costs that do not show up in the drug budget. Excess hip fractures have reached about sixteen thousand a year. Medicare's drug spending stayed flat while its fracture costs grew, and the two sit in different budgets. The free program does not require a bone scan.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renee Alvarado, fifty-two, picks up her semaglutide at the Walmart on Power Road in Mesa before work. It costs $44.18, and the receipt prints longer than the box. Until January her dental office's plan paid for Zepbound. Then the plan letter said 'cardiometabolic codes only', and her A1c is fine. She lost three weeks switching and gained nine pounds. Her mother's Medicare generic costs nothing, which is the first thing her mother says on every call.

At the office the hygienist, Kayla, is eating a burrito the size of a forearm and saying she is 'proudly unmedicated'. She shows Renee her lean-mass printout like a report card.

At lunch Renee's husband Dale texts a photo of a blister pack. It is the Wegovy pill, free on her plan because it is for cigarettes. He has been at it for six weeks and has smoked two. 'Covered till August,' he writes. 'Then I start the second quit.'

At four, her neighbour Marisol drops off a cooler bag of unlabelled vials. They came from an Arizona 'peptide clinic' her son found, and she has taken out what she owed Renee for the tomatoes. Renee does not open the bag. She puts it in the garage fridge next to the Topo Chico and decides she has not decided yet.

She skips Friday's dose because it is her niece's quinceañera. At the party she eats two plates of birria and dances until her feet hurt. Driving home, Dale says she seemed like herself. She asks him who that is, and they both laugh. She is not sure the question was a joke.
